newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London traded within narrow ranges of no more than $1.90 on any position and business was routine with no dominant feature to the listless session. December gave up 40 cents to close at $313.80 and March was 90 cents down at $309.50. In New York raw sugar futures ended a thinly-traded session barely below unchanged. The March contract finished under support seen around 10.50 cents/lb at 10.47 cents/lb, an indication of possible weakness Thursday. May ended 2 points lower at 10.54 cents/lb. Without fresh physical demand prices are likely to lose further ground.

IRAN - According to industry sources sugar production in 1996/97 is likely to fall to 723,000 tonnes, raw value, down from 938,000 tonnes produced in 1995/96 and 899,000 tonnes in 1994/95. Of the total in 1996/97 552,000 tonnes (737,000 tonnes) is expected to be beet sugar and 171,000 tonnes (201,000 tonnes) cane sugar.

AUSTRALIA - According to industry sources sugar production in 1996/97 is forecast to rise by 9.7 percent to 5.491 million tonnes (94 net titre) up from 5.006 million tonnes produced in 1995/96 and 5.064 million tonnes in 1994/95.

FRANCE - Sugar imports in August 1996 amounted to 11,448 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 28,332 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first 11 months of 1995/96 (October/August) up to 436,251 tonnes against 338,900 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 364,140 tonnes, down from 389,982 tonnes in 1993/94. Major suppliers of raws in October/August 1995/96 were Reunion with 158,481 tonnes against 139,842 tonnes, Swaziland with 53,962 tonnes compared to 50,172 tonnes and Guadeloupe with 25,679 tonnes against 25,657 tonnes. The largest suppliers of white sugar were Belgium-Luxembourg with 34,575 tonnes against 12,495 tonnes and Germany with 26,520 tonnes compared to 18,774 tonnes. Sugar exports in August 1996 amounted to 192,299 tonnes against 221,814 tonnes in August 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/August 1995/96 up to 2.71 million tonnes, down from 2.94 million tonnes exported in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 3.07 million tonnes against 2.82 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/August 1995/96 were Belgium-Luxembourg with 461,008 tonnes whites against 928,580 tonnes, Spain with 228,478 tonnes, up from 198,157 tonnes, Turkey with 219,907 tonnes against 102,358 tonnes and Iran with 176,836 tonnes against 196,012 tonnes.

The European Union awarded 104,950 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 46.220 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to October 30 reached 811,600 tonnes, which compares to 1,031,755 tonnes last year.
